title: Things to Do in Varaždin, Croatia: Top Attractions 2027
metaDescription: Top things to do in Varaždin: Old Town castle, Main Square, baroque churches, the cemetery, Špancirfest and Advent, with prices, hours and tips.
content:
## Why Varaždin Is Worth a Visit

Varaždin is a city of about 47,000 people in northern Croatia, roughly 81 km north of Zagreb. It served as the capital of Croatia from 1756 to 1776, and a large fire in 1776 led to a rebuild in baroque and rococo style. That is why the centre looks like a small Central European capital, and why the city is nicknamed "Little Vienna". The historic core is pedestrian-friendly, and the main sights sit within about 10 minutes' walk of each other.

## Old Town Castle and Varaždin City Museum

The Old Town (Stari Grad) is the city's best-known landmark. It is a Gothic-Renaissance fortress with white walls, corner towers and a moat. It stands at the northern edge of the centre, on Strossmayerovo šetalište. The complex dates from the 14th to 17th centuries. The city bought it from the Erdödy family in 1925 and opened the City Museum inside it the same year.

### What You See Inside

The cultural-history department shows furnished rooms in period styles: Renaissance, Baroque, Rococo, Empire, Biedermeier and Art Deco. Collections include weapons, portraits, clocks, glass, porcelain and guild objects. The courtyard, with its arcaded galleries, is worth a visit even if you skip the rooms.

### Hours and Tickets

- Tuesday to Friday: 9:00–17:00
- Saturday and Sunday: 9:00–13:00
- Closed Mondays and public holidays
- Last admission is 30 minutes before closing
- Adult entry is roughly €5–7

The castle has been under renovation, and interior access has been limited. Check the City Museum's current status before planning around it. The grounds, moat and embankment path are free to walk at any time.

## Main Square and Town Hall

Trg kralja Tomislava is the centre of town. The Town Hall dates from the 1500s and was rebuilt in the 18th century. It is one of the oldest city halls in Croatia still in use. Colourful baroque facades surround it, and the Patačić Palace and the cafés along the square are all close by.

The ceremonial Guard of Varaždin (Purgari) changes in front of the Town Hall on Saturdays at 11:00 in the summer season. Dates vary, so confirm them locally.

### Pedestrian Streets Around the Square

From the Main Square, Franjevački trg, Gundulićeva and Kapucinski trg lead into the car-free core. Coffee costs about €1.80–2.50 on the square. Prices on side streets are slightly lower.

## Churches: Cathedral and Franciscan Church

The Cathedral of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a 17th-century baroque building, originally a Jesuit church. It became a cathedral in 1997. Its gilded main altar and ceiling frescoes are the main features, and entry is free outside services.

The Franciscan Church of St. John the Baptist is on Franjevački trg, close to the Main Square. It is known for its tall bell tower, one of the tallest in Croatia. In front of it stands a copy of Ivan Meštrović's Grgur Ninski statue. Rubbing the statue's toe is a local custom said to bring luck.

## Sermage Palace and Other Museums

Sermage Palace holds the Gallery of Old and Contemporary Masters. It is a rococo-baroque building with period interiors and a European painting collection. The Herzer Palace houses the entomological collection, and the Watchtower is part of the Old Town complex. Museum hours generally follow the City Museum pattern, so Mondays are a poor day for indoor sightseeing. Combine museum visits on Tuesday to Friday, when hours run to 17:00.

## Varaždin Cemetery

The Varaždin Cemetery is a landscaped park of about 18 hectares. It was designed by the architect Hermann Haller and opened in 1905. Its main feature is the clipped hedges and tree-lined alleys, shaped into walls, arches and geometric forms. Entry is free and it is open daily, with longer hours in summer. It is about 1.3 km from the Main Square, a 15-minute walk.

The cemetery deserves more of your time than most castle rooms do. It is the one sight in town with no equivalent elsewhere in Croatia, so allow 60 to 90 minutes. Visit respectfully, since it is still an active burial ground.

## Špancirfest: The Headline Festival

Špancirfest is a ten-day street festival, held in late August. The 2026 edition ran 21–30 August with about 600 programmes across 23 zones in the historic centre. It includes street performers, concerts, theatre, workshops and food stalls. The main PAN stage stands beneath the Old Town. Most of the programme is free. Only selected concerts at Villa Bedeković require tickets. Expect the 2027 edition in late August as well, but confirm dates on the festival's official site.

Accommodation fills up fast during the festival, so book several weeks ahead. If crowds are a concern, the days before the final weekend are noticeably calmer.

## Varaždin Advent

The Advent market runs from late November to early January. In the 2026–27 season it was scheduled from 28 November to 6 January. It includes stalls on the squares, lights across the centre and an ice rink. Rink entry costs around €4–5, and skate hire adds about €2–3. Weekday mornings are the quietest time, though some stalls open only later in the afternoon.

## Other Headline Events

Varaždin Baroque Evenings, a classical music festival, takes place in autumn. It runs in churches, palaces and the Old Town. The City Museum extends its opening hours for it and for the Night of Museums.

## How to Plan One Day in Varaždin

1. Morning: Old Town grounds and museum (9:00–11:30).
2. Late morning: Franciscan Church, Cathedral and Main Square.
3. Lunch: a restaurant on or near the Main Square.
4. Afternoon: Sermage Palace or the City Museum departments.
5. Late afternoon: Varaždin Cemetery, with light good for walking until sunset.

For Saturday visits, go early. The museums close at 13:00, and the guard change at 11:00 fits between them.

## Practical Tips

- **Getting there:** Zagreb to Varaždin is about 81 km, roughly 1 hour 15 minutes by car. Trains and buses also run from Zagreb. The station is about 1 km from the centre.
- **Getting around:** The centre is flat and compact. Walking covers everything. Bicycles are common locally.
- **Best seasons:** Late spring and early autumn have mild weather and fewer crowds. August suits festival visitors. December suits Advent visitors.
- **Local tip:** Mondays are the weakest day for museums. Use them for the cemetery, church visits and walking the squares instead.
- **Local tip:** Eat a slice of Varaždin klipić (a local crescent-shaped bread roll) from a bakery. Locals buy them as a morning snack.

## Frequently Searched Questions

See the FAQ below for short answers on tickets, time needed and festival dates.

faq.question: What are the top things to do in Varaždin?
faq.answer: The main sights are the Old Town castle and City Museum, the Main Square with its Town Hall, the Cathedral and Franciscan church, Sermage Palace and the Varaždin Cemetery. In late August, Špancirfest is the biggest event of the year. Most of these sights are within a 10–15 minute walk of each other.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Varaždin?
faq.answer: One full day covers the main attractions: castle, churches, Main Square, a museum and the cemetery. Add a second day if you want a slower pace, or if you visit during Špancirfest or Advent.

faq.question: How much does Varaždin Castle cost to enter?
faq.answer: Adult entry to the castle museum is roughly €5–7. The grounds and moat path are free. Opening hours are Tuesday to Friday 9:00–17:00 and weekends 9:00–13:00, closed Mondays. Check whether interior renovation affects access before you go.

faq.question: Is Varaždin Cemetery free to visit?
faq.answer: Yes, entry is free and the cemetery is open daily. It was designed by Hermann Haller and opened in 1905. It is known for its clipped hedges and landscaped alleys, and visitors should keep quiet because it is still in use.

faq.question: When is Špancirfest in Varaždin?
faq.answer: Špancirfest is held in late August and lasts ten days. The 2026 edition ran from 21 to 30 August. Most of the street programme is free, and only certain concerts at Villa Bedeković need tickets.

faq.question: Is Varaždin worth visiting from Zagreb?
faq.answer: Yes. It is about 81 km from Zagreb and offers a baroque centre, a fortress and an unusual cemetery. A single day is enough to see the main sights.

faq.question: When does the Varaždin Advent market run?
faq.answer: The Advent market runs from late November to early January. In 2026–27 it was scheduled from 28 November to 6 January. Ice rink entry costs about €4–5, with skate hire at €2–3.

quickAnswer: The top things to do in Varaždin are the Old Town castle and City Museum, the baroque Main Square and Town Hall, the Cathedral and Franciscan church, the Varaždin Cemetery, and Špancirfest in late August. The compact centre is walkable in one day, and the cemetery is free.
